## Origin

**Pili-pili** (also piri-piri) names the hot chili and, by extension, the sauce that goes with it across Central and Southern Africa. In the DRC it is not a brand: it is the table condiment — local chilies, garlic, sometimes tomato — dosed household by household. The word circulates in Lingala and Swahili as much as in Kinshasa French.

## At the table

Pili-pili sauce is not a main dish: it is the table’s heat. Tomato softens, lemon brightens. Serve with [grilled chicken](/en/recettes/soso-ya-kotumba/), [ntaba](/en/recettes/ntaba/), [braised fish](/en/recettes/poisson-braise-kinkole/) or [kamundele](/en/recettes/kamundele/).

**Beans with nguba** (peanut) are the Kasai peanut gesture on legumes—cousins of Western [madesu](/en/recettes/madesu/) and Eastern [maharage](/en/recettes/haricots-maharage/) (more tomato). Sauce alone: [peanut sauce](/en/recettes/sauce-arachide/).

**Beef moambe** uses the same palm sauce as [chicken moambe](/en/recettes/moambe-poulet/) and [fish moambe](/en/recettes/poisson-moambe/)—longer simmer, same patience. Natural sides: [rice with moambe](/en/recettes/riz-moambe/) or [pondu](/en/recettes/pondu/).

**Beef skewers** at the table are more generous than [kamundele](/en/recettes/kamundele/) (tiny street cubes). Other grilled beef: [boeuf ya kotumba](/en/recettes/boeuf-ya-kotumba/). Liver: [liver skewers](/en/recettes/brochettes-foie/).
**Boiled maize** is the water gesture; [grilled maize](/en/recettes/mais-grille/) goes on the fire. Creamy snack: [maize porridge](/en/recettes/bouillie-mais/).

**Braised capitaine fish** (Nile perch) is the river grillade when the market has a large piece. The [Kinkole braised fish](/en/recettes/poisson-braise-kinkole/) page stays the generic street gesture; here species and size set the cooking time.

**Caramel bananas** are the pan dessert; [banana fritters](/en/recettes/beignets-banane/) go through the fryer, [steamed sweet bananas](/en/recettes/bananes-douces-vapeur/) stay plain. Savoury fried plantain: [makemba](/en/recettes/makemba/).

**Cassava fries** are not [grilled cassava](/en/recettes/manioc-grille/) (coals) nor [cassava fritters](/en/recettes/beignets-manioc/) (batter). Other fry: [fried sweet potato](/en/recettes/patate-douce-frite/), [cassava croquettes](/en/recettes/croquettes-manioc/).

**Chicken skewers** are the stick snack; [soso ya kotumba](/en/recettes/soso-ya-kotumba/) remains chicken in pieces. Beef cousins: [beef skewers](/en/recettes/brochettes-boeuf/), [kamundele](/en/recettes/kamundele/).
**Dried meat** travels well on the Katanga plateaus—like [kapenta](/en/recettes/kapenta-tomates/) on the lake side. Fresh cousin in sauce: [viande ya sauce](/en/recettes/viande-ya-sauce/).

**Fried sweet potato** is the fry gesture; [mbala](/en/recettes/mbala/) is mostly boiled, [grilled mbala](/en/recettes/mbala-grillee/) goes on the fire. Fry cousins: [cassava fries](/en/recettes/manioc-frites/), [makemba](/en/recettes/makemba/).

**Grilled maize** is the coal snack; [boiled maize](/en/recettes/mais-bouilli/) stays in water, [maize porridge](/en/recettes/bouillie-mais/) is the creamy snack. Maize flour paste: [bukari / bugali](/en/recettes/bukari-katanga/).

**Grilled ngolo** is the coal-fire catfish plate; [pepe soupe ya ngolo](/en/recettes/pepe-soupe-ya-ngolo/) is the soup version. Other river braise: [Kinkole braised fish](/en/recettes/poisson-braise-kinkole/). Fried: [mbisi ya kokalinga](/en/recettes/mbisi-ya-kokalinga/).

**Grilled shrimp** are the coal gesture; [river shrimp in sauce](/en/recettes/crevettes-fleuve/) simmer. Other small / dried crustacean: [kossa-kossa](/en/recettes/kossa-kossa/). Coal fish: [Kinkole](/en/recettes/poisson-braise-kinkole/).

**Kinshasa cabbage** is the capital cousin of [Eastern simmered cabbage](/en/recettes/chou-mijote-est/): same vegetable, more often palm oil and cube. Crunchy salad in another city: [Kisangani salad](/en/recettes/salade-kisangani/). Leaf green: [ndunda](/en/recettes/ndunda/).

**Kinshasa spaghetti** borrows the Italian pasta shape for a local tomato-onion sauce — urban cousin of [loso mayonnaise](/en/recettes/loso-mayonnaise/) and [loso na madesu](/en/recettes/loso-na-madesu/). Another quick plate: [sausage and fries](/en/recettes/saucisse-frites/).

**Kisangani fish** is the city’s simmered river-market plate: less pure grill than [Kinkole braised fish](/en/recettes/poisson-braise-kinkole/), saucier than [grilled ngolo](/en/recettes/ngolo-grille/). Same local table: [Kisangani salad](/en/recettes/salade-kisangani/).

**Lait caillé** at home stays a short, controlled lactic set — not a careless ferment. Other creamy snacks: [peanut porridge](/en/recettes/bouillie-arachide/), [maize porridge](/en/recettes/bouillie-mais/). Fruit dessert: [caramel bananas](/en/recettes/bananes-caramel/).

**Makosso** (pork trotters in sauce) is a family sharing dish. In Kasai it often meets **potatoes**—a highland starch, cousin to [grilled mbala](/en/recettes/mbala-grillee/). Other pork in sauce: [ngulu ya sauce](/en/recettes/ngulu-ya-sauce/).

**Malafu** (palm wine) is a western / Kongo-Central drink, often sold fresh along the road. This sheet covers **serving** and pairings — like other fermented drinks in the catalogue ([munkoyo](/en/recettes/munkoyo/)), without an extraction guide. Non-alcoholic table drink: [bissap juice](/en/recettes/jus-bissap/).

**Mikila with peanut** keeps the oxtail of [mikila](/en/recettes/mikila/) (tomato sauce) but follows [peanut sauce](/en/recettes/sauce-arachide/) logic. Long cook, melting collagen — feast or diaspora table.

**Mushroom liboke** applies the [fish liboke](/en/recettes/liboke-poisson/) technique to seasonal mushrooms — packet, not pot. Open sauce: [mayebo with tomatoes](/en/recettes/mayebo/). Other Bandundu plate: [mbinzo with tomatoes](/en/recettes/mbinzo-tomates/).

**Nsafu in sauce** carries safou season past the snack: [grilled nsafu](/en/recettes/nsafu-grilles/) stay the coal gesture; here the buttery pulp binds a short sauce. Seasonal drink: [safou juice](/en/recettes/jus-safou/).

**Peanut cake** carries nguba flavour in sweet form — distinct from [peanut porridge](/en/recettes/bouillie-arachide/) and [cassava cake](/en/recettes/gateau-manioc/). Crunchy confection: [peanut sweets](/en/recettes/bonbons-arachide/).
**Peanut sweets** are the crunchy take; [peanut cake](/en/recettes/gateau-arachide/) stays a soft bake. Careful with very hot caramel. Other fried snack: [mikate](/en/recettes/mikate/).

**Pig trotters** (Lingala: *makoso*) are a patient feast dish: long-simmered, often spicy, served in a fragrant broth. Some tables treat it like pepper soup; others like it thicker with tomato. With potatoes: [makosso with potatoes](/en/recettes/makosso-pommes/). Chili soup cousin: [pepe soup with catfish](/en/recettes/pepe-soupe-ya-ngolo/).

**Plantain fufu** (close to banana foutou) is a **pounded paste**, not [lituma](/en/recettes/lituma/) mash nor fried [makemba](/en/recettes/makemba/). Other paste: [cassava fufu](/en/recettes/fufu-manioc/). Plain steam: [steamed plantains](/en/recettes/plantains-vapeur/).

**Pork ribs** play the bone-in cut; [braised pork](/en/recettes/porc-braise/) often starts from shoulder/loin, [porc ya kotumba](/en/recettes/porc-ya-kotumba/) targets the grilled snack. In sauce: [ngulu ya sauce](/en/recettes/ngulu-ya-sauce/).

**River shrimp** show up when the river market is good. Another small dried seafood in the catalogue: [kossa-kossa](/en/recettes/kossa-kossa/). Fish papillote: [liboke fish](/en/recettes/liboke-poisson/).
**Sambousa** (samosas) with potato are a **Goma** and Swahili-speaking East snack—seller photo on Commons. Fried cousins: [andazi](/en/recettes/andazi-tanganyika/), [mikate](/en/recettes/mikate/).

**Simmered tripe** sits among Kinshasa offal plates beside [sautéed beef liver](/en/recettes/foie-boeuf-saute/) and [liver skewers](/en/recettes/brochettes-foie/). Another long offal simmer: [makosso](/en/recettes/makosso-pommes/).

**Tamarind juice** plays fruity tartness where [bissap](/en/recettes/jus-bissap/) leans floral and [tangawisi](/en/recettes/tangawisi/) leans ginger. Market block pulp or concentrate: adjust water and sugar.

**Tangawisi juice** (ginger juice) is drunk iced, often after a spicy meal. Ginger and sugar levels vary widely. Other drinks: [bissap](/en/recettes/jus-bissap/), [mango juice](/en/recettes/jus-mangue/), [tamarind juice](/en/recettes/jus-tamarin/). Pair with [mikate](/en/recettes/mikate/) at snack time.

**Taro in peanut sauce** shares the tuber with [simmered taro](/en/recettes/taro-mijote/) (tomato sauce) but follows [peanut sauce](/en/recettes/sauce-arachide/) logic. Yam cousin: [yam in sauce](/en/recettes/igname-sauce/).

**Vegetable liboke** applies the [fish liboke](/en/recettes/liboke-poisson/) and [meat liboke](/en/recettes/liboke-viande/) technique to a vegetable filling—useful on meatless days. Another eggplant plate: [African eggplants in sauce](/en/recettes/aubergines-africaines/).

**Yam in sauce** extends [boiled yam](/en/recettes/igname-bouillie/): same tuber, tomato sauce that carries the plate. Other simmered tuber: [simmered taro](/en/recettes/taro-mijote/). Fried snack: [yam fritters](/en/recettes/beignets-igname/).
